skill.name: image-edit
skill.description: Routes image edit requests to the best RunComfy model for batch edits, text rewrites, multi-reference composition, local edits, and mask-based inpainting.
skill.summary: Route image edit requests to the right RunComfy model and CLI command.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The confirmed static findings are expected RunComfy CLI invocations and setup commands, not hidden code execution. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, placeholder URLs, and documented token storage. Semantic review found no prompt-injection text in the skill, but remote processing and untrusted image inputs create privacy and model-injection risks.

remediation.issue: RunComfy CLI commands process user prompts and image URLs through a remote service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running the CLI and clearly show which URLs, prompts, and output directory will be used.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on third-party image and mask URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Document that input URLs must be trusted, public HTTPS assets and warn users not to send confidential images or private signed URLs.

remediation.issue: The RunComfy login flow stores an API token on disk unless RUNCOMFY_TOKEN is used.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment-based tokens for CI, document token revocation, and keep the token file owner-readable only.

remediation.issue: Generated outputs are downloaded to a user-selected directory.
remediation.suggestion: Validate output directories before execution and avoid writing generated files outside the active project or an approved output folder.

content.user_title: Edit Images with RunComfy Model Routing
content.value_statement: Image edit requests often need different models for text, masks, batches, and local changes. This skill routes each request to a matching RunComfy edit model.
actual_capabilities: Routes edit requests across Nano Banana Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, Flux Kontext Pro, and Z-Image Turbo Inpaint.
Prepares RunComfy CLI commands with the model-specific input fields required by each route.
Supports batch edit guidance for up to 20 input image URLs with locked aspect ratio and resolution options.
Guides multilingual in-image text rewrites and multi-reference composition with numbered source images.
Supports mask-driven object removal and region replacement using grayscale mask image URLs.
Provides prompt patterns for preservation, spatial scope, text replacement, and small iterative edits.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a RunComfy account or API token before use.
Uses publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs rather than direct local image files.
Selects one model per call and does not blend multiple routes in a single request.
Output quality, latency, and accepted parameters depend on the selected RunComfy model.

use_cases.title: Prepare Campaign Image Variants
use_cases.description: Create consistent visual variants while preserving subject identity, layout, or brand elements across a batch.

use_cases.title: Clean Product Photos
use_cases.description: Remove distractions, replace backgrounds, or produce consistent catalog images using batch and mask-based routes.

use_cases.title: Localize In-Image Text
use_cases.description: Rewrite poster or product image text in another language while keeping the original design and brand mark.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this image with RunComfy. Keep the subject identity, pose, clothing, and framing unchanged. Replace only the background with a clean studio setting.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Product Refresh
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit these product image URLs as a batch. Keep each product unchanged. Replace the background with light gray studio paper and use the same square format for every result.

prompt_templates.title: Localized Poster Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the best RunComfy route for text replacement. Keep the photo, layout, colors, and logo unchanged. Replace only the headline with the provided translated text.

prompt_templates.title: Masked Object Removal
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mask-driven inpainting route. Remove the masked object, preserve the unmasked surroundings, match nearby texture, and keep the final image natural.

output_examples.input: A user provides one portrait URL and asks for a rainy neon street background without changing the person.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Nano Banana Edit and prepares a preservation-first edit request for the RunComfy CLI.

output_examples.input: A user provides a poster URL and asks to replace the English headline with Japanese text.
output_examples.output: The skill selects GPT Image 2 Edit and frames the request to preserve layout, brand mark, typography position, and image content.

output_examples.input: A user provides a street image URL and a grayscale cable mask URL for object removal.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo Inpaint and recommends low-strength inpainting that preserves rooflines and sky gradients.

best_practices: State the elements that must stay unchanged before describing the edit.
Use publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs and verify masks before starting an inpainting request.
Split complex changes into smaller passes when identity, text, or layout must remain stable.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated edits, text rewrites, and background changes in one vague request.
Do not use private local file paths where the selected RunComfy model expects public image URLs.
Do not use mask-based inpainting without checking that white and black mask regions are correct.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It chooses a RunComfy image edit model based on the requested edit and prepares the matching CLI request.

faq.question: Which models can it route to?
faq.answer: It can route to Nano Banana Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, Flux Kontext Pro, and Z-Image Turbo Inpaint.

faq.question: Does it support batch image edits?
faq.answer: Yes. The Nano Banana route supports guidance for batches of up to 20 input image URLs.

faq.question: Can it edit text inside images?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes multilingual and layout-sensitive in-image text edits to GPT Image 2 Edit.

faq.question: Does it need a mask for every edit?
faq.answer: No. Masks are required only for the Z-Image Turbo Inpaint route.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and either a login session or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.
